extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (api.tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Long titles are no longer cut off on the home screen and the details page. Where something has no logo artwork of its own, tofa shows its name as text -- and that text was set so large that a long name ran most of the way across the screen and was still cut short. It is smaller now and wraps onto a second line, so you get the whole name. - tofa asks once more to add its fonts to your skin, because the change above needed a text size it had not installed before. It is the same one-off question as always and Kodi restarts straight after; nothing else changes. - Subtitles that came with a DVD or Blu-ray rip as separate files now play properly. Where a film's subtitles sit in a pair of files beside it rather than inside it, tofa used to either re-encode the whole picture to paint them on -- costing quality -- or not offer them at all. They are now sent across as they are and drawn on top, so the picture is untouched. Needs tofa server 0.9.32. - Video your server has to convert on the way to you can now arrive as HEVC instead of H.264, which holds more detail at the same bandwidth. tofa had never said it could take anything but H.264, so it always got the older one. This applies only to conversion -- anything that plays untouched is unaffected -- and only once whoever runs your server has switched HEVC on for it, which is off to begin with. - This version needs tofa server 0.9.32 or newer. On an older server the disc-rip subtitles above will not appear and converted video keeps coming as H.264; everything else works as before.

extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - After you finish an episode, the details page now describes the NEXT episode, not the one you just watched. The Play button already moved on to the next episode, but the synopsis and the audio and video badges stayed behind on the one that had just ended. - Settings now tells you how this device is reaching your server: connected directly, or through tofa's relay. On the relay everything travels through tofa, video included, so it can be slower -- and until now nothing on screen said which one you were on. - The Account page in Settings fills in the moment it opens. It used to leave the panel blank for a beat while it waited on one slower lookup before showing anything.

extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - A series now carries on from where you are. If you had finished a later episode but skipped one earlier on, the details page went back and offered the skipped one instead of the episode you were up to. - Something you have finished no longer offers both Play and Rewatch. Both started it from the beginning, so there was nothing to choose between them. - Playback statistics now report the soundtrack's own channels. Where sound is passed straight through to an amplifier, a 5.1 soundtrack was described as 7.1: the panel was reading the connection carrying the sound rather than the sound itself.

extension.summary: Install and update the tofa add-on
extension.description: The update channel for tofa's Kodi add-on. Installing this repository lets Kodi fetch the add-on and every later release on its own.
